question: Your team runs named research sessions with --resume, in which the document analysis subagent builds findings from a corpus of 50 source reports. A teammate proposes a standard step for resumed work: the resume message lists the specific reports that changed and asks the session to re-analyze only those reports. Your lead wants to know when this step is the right choice. In which situation does this step fit best?

options.text: Most of the 50 reports were replaced with new editions, so nearly all of the tool results stored in the named session are now stale.
options.reason: When prior tool results are stale, the guide says a new session with an injected structured summary is more reliable than resuming, so targeted re-analysis inside the old session is the wrong choice.

options.text: No reports changed since the last work session, and the team simply wants to continue the same investigation the next day with all earlier findings intact.
options.reason: With no changed files, there is nothing to re-analyze, and the guide's plain --resume with the session name already continues the named investigation across work sessions.

options.text: The team wants to compare two different synthesis approaches that both start from the same completed analysis of the 50 reports, without one approach affecting the other.
options.reason: The guide uses fork_session to create independent branches from a shared analysis baseline to explore divergent approaches, so this need calls for forking, not a list of changed reports.

options.text: Two of the 50 reports received corrected editions, and the earlier analysis of the other 48 reports in the named session is still valid.
options.reason: Prior context is mostly valid, so resuming fits, and the guide says to tell the resumed session about the specific file changes for targeted re-analysis instead of full re-exploration.
